reason: Design plan frozen. Requirements and evaluation contract read; Python os.replace passage verified. Linux rename(2) retrieval failed through web access and curl DNS resolution; its decisive passages remain a required evidence gap before completion.
goal: Compare two mechanisms for a single-process JSON checkpoint and produce a conditional, source-grounded recommendation with independent review.
baseline: A: directly truncate and rewrite the checkpoint file. B: write complete JSON to a temporary file on the destination filesystem, close it, then publish with os.replace.
constraints: Purpose is design; no efficacy experiment or performance claim.
Two-candidate exception: the requirements explicitly limit the decision to these two real mechanisms; additional methods would expand the question.
Use only the fixture requirements and decisive Python os.replace and Linux rename(2) primary passages.
Python evidence: https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.replace, decisive passage at lines 1833–1836 confirms atomic rename on success and possible cross-filesystem failure.
Linux evidence pending: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/rename.2.html, DESCRIPTION replacement semantics and ERRORS EXDEV.
Do not treat atomic visibility as a power-loss durability guarantee; the named sources cannot establish a complete durability protocol.
No checks executed, files modified, packages installed, memory written, commits or deployments.
Examples are illustrative reasoning, not measured outcomes; retain retrieval failures and unknowns.

criteria.title: Conditional mechanism choice
criteria.acceptance: Compare A and B and condition the recommendation on preserving a complete checkpoint during interrupted updates versus accepting checkpoint loss for simpler writes. Explain both mechanisms without claiming measured effectiveness.

criteria.title: Atomic publication scope
criteria.acceptance: Ground successful replacement semantics in the decisive Python and Linux passages. Distinguish publication of a completed temporary file from atomicity of its preceding writes; explain that existing open descriptors can retain the old file.

criteria.title: Durability boundary
criteria.acceptance: Separate atomic pathname visibility from persistence after power loss or system crash. State that durability is unmeasured and a complete synchronization protocol is not established by these passages.

criteria.title: Filesystem constraint
criteria.acceptance: Verify Linux EXDEV and Python's cross-filesystem warning; require the temporary file on the destination filesystem, preferably in its directory. Do not present a cross-filesystem copy fallback as atomic replacement.

criteria.title: Independent evidence review
criteria.acceptance: An independent reviewer checks the final explanation against the original decisive passages and R1–R4, retaining unsupported claims and source gaps as unresolved. Completion requires the Linux source gap to be closed.

complexity_baseline: A uses one destination write sequence. B adds temporary-file lifecycle and a replacement operation. Compare these structural costs qualitatively; no timing or reliability measurement.
